claude.country: Multiple low- and middle-income countries (23 institutions, IAEA); cases from Denmark

links.outcome: Contour quality (DSC) and time for radiation oncologists with vs without AI-assisted contouring
links.effect: AI assistance raised DSC for optic nerve (0.05), oral cavity (0.10), parotid (0.07), spinal cord (0.04), mandible (0.02) and cut contouring time (e.g., mandible -6.60 min); 24% of AI contours accepted unedited.
links.quote: Regardless of teaching, AI-assisted contouring increased contouring quality and reduced contouring time for most investigated OARs.

links.outcome: Clinician performance using AI in intended workflow versus manual contouring
links.effect: Randomized comparison showed higher DSC vs expert consensus and lower time with AI-assisted contouring; outliers (DSC<0.4) 2.5% manual vs 0.2% AI-assisted.
links.quote: With an (arbitrary) threshold in DSC at 0.4, 2.5% of manual contours and only 0.2% of AI-assisted contours were outliers.

links.outcome: Possible automation bias in accepting AI contours without editing
links.effect: 335 (24%) AI contours accepted without editing by 66 (68%) participants; authors say automation bias may be at play, and the effect of erroneous AI contours is unknown.
links.quote: The fact that two thirds of participants handed in all the accepted-as-is-contours suggests either that automation bias was at play for these participants or that these participants might have cognitively processed the review of AI contours differently.

links.outcome: Randomized evaluation of AI benefit on contour quality/time (not patient outcomes)
links.effect: Randomized trial showed improved surrogate outcomes, but contours were not used clinically; authors call for prospective clinical studies.
links.quote: A major limitation to the study was that contours were not used clinically.

links.outcome: Effect of a teaching session on contouring quality and time savings with AI
links.effect: Teaching increased DSC for only two OARs without AI, but increased AI time savings (e.g., mandible -9.41 min with teaching vs -6.60 without); effect persisted at 6 months.
links.quote: Although teaching did not increase contouring quality as much as expected, teaching modified the time savings of AI-assisted contouring; for most OARs, AI-assisted contouring alone reduced contouring time (crosses, Fig 5 ), but even larger time savings were observed when AI-assisted contouring was combined with teaching (lines, Fig 5 ).
